_doc: Input of make_done_exclusions.py: the short list of MEMOS #70 (3), designs that may stay out of the DoD-5 band (exact or at most make_compare_csv.BAND_OVER over: 5 % since 2026-10-24, MEMOS #95; 15 % before), each with its per-array cause, the Vitis evidence and why it is out of scope. 'status' says whether Peter has accepted the entry (citing his decision); 'proposed' entries come from a prove report and wait for him. '_withdrawn' keeps entries taken off the list, with the reason; the script ignores it.

entries.cause: `weights` 0 against Vitis 3 (-3): Vitis keeps 3 of the 9 per-node m_axi row copies of the struct-member table (`array<WT_TYPE, EMB_DIM> weights[ND_FEATURE]`, 80 x 16 banks) and forwards the other 6; hls-est does not split the nested struct member (O169) and would price all 9 (+6) if it did. Offset by `accs_ping` / `accs_pong` +1 each (O187: the conditional row view is not lowered, so the loop stays sequential and both stay 1-BRAM memories where Vitis partitions them into registers): net -1 of 20,600 (-0.005 %)
entries.vitis_evidence: VITIS_NOTES N149 (W9r20-prove): the six missing `weights` rows are removed by GVN store-to-load forwarding inside MemDep's block scan window, which Vitis' front end sets to 1000 instructions (Xilinx's own default: `cl::init(1000)` in hls-llvm-project's MemoryDependenceAnalysis.cpp:86-89, upstream LLVM 100); re-running Vitis' own reflow front end on pna's cached bitcode reproduces the 3 kept rows, and -mllvm -memdep-block-scan-limit=500 / 900 / 1100 / 2000 gives 6 / 4 / 2 / 0 (pm9f: an explicit 1000 reproduces the default load for load, 100 does not). N146 (13 kernels w9r19p_pm* / pf_*): pna's loading loop is not pipelined ([SCHED 204-61], hls_compile.log:953); the kernels keep 0 0 0 0 1 4 8 9 10 12 of NF = 2 ... 12 rows, pna's function standalone 5 of 9, 9 without its stream write
entries.why_out_of_scope: the kept-row count is a function of the instruction counts of Vitis' intermediate LLVM IR at each of its front-end GVN runs (after unroll, inline, ap_fixed library inlining, array partition and m_axi lowering) and of which loads earlier runs erased; hls-est's MLIR has no counterpart for those counts, so any window in MLIR ops would be fitted to pna, not a rule. Fixing O187 alone makes pna -3 (further out); pricing all 9 rows makes it +6 (in band, wrong per array)
entries.status: accepted by Peter, 2026-10-24 (MEMOS #94); entry from W9r19-prove / W9r19-impl, evidence completed W9r20-prove

_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: VITIS_NOTES N120 (pengzhao `loadA_Stage`: startA in state 11, endA in state 12, ram_1p 1; kernel w9r15p_rp_pipe puts them in one state, = hls-est); OPEN_ISSUES O66 (b)
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: both parts lack a proven rule (the endA delay, the stream element width of a struct); the net -1 is the sum of +1 and -2
_withdrawn.status: proposed (W9r16-impl 2026-10-23; waiting for Peter, not accepted)
_withdrawn.withdrawn: W9 round 18 review fixes (2026-10-24): the FIFO half is proven (VITIS_NOTES N141: a function-static struct stream is sizeof * 8 bits wide; ArowStream / CrowStream 6 = Vitis), so the design is 32 against Vitis 31 (+3.2 %, in band); the remaining +1 is local_rowPtrA (N120, unconfirmed)

_withdrawn.cause: conv1d_2 / conv1d_3 / conv1d_4: Vitis does not flatten the parent loop with its auto-pipelined child ([HLS 200-960] '... either the parent loop or sub loop is do-while loop'), so the child runs alone at II 1 and the temp_* weights are RAM_1WNR with 4 copies; hls-est flattens, gets II 10 and RAM_2P (-156); the remaining -3 is a register-sized array
_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: VITIS_NOTES N64 (11 kernels w9r8p_*) and N76 (9 kernels w9r9p_n64_*): the refusal does not depend on the parent's trip count (92/64), the element type (float/int), the nesting depth (x loop removed) or the child's trip (5/3); it disappears with an explicit pipeline on the child (n64_cpipe) or an explicit unroll on the grandchild (n64_kunr), and with an if on c or k inside the grandchild (n64_ifconly / n64_ifkonly), but not with an if on l + k (n64_iflonly, the ECG shape) or without an if (dw_noif); in every refused kernel db/a.o.1.ll has the parent l in do-while form with the hoisted address l + 1 as its increment
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: candidate rule (N76, unconfirmed): a parent is not flattened when its child is pipelined only by the automatic pipeline (214-376), the child holds a sub-loop that only that pipeline unrolls (214-291), and no condition on the child's or sub-loop's index guards the sub-loop body; it is backed by 13 kernels but its two flattening exceptions (if on c / k) are not derived from a mechanism, and 10 of the 14 corpus designs with this warning are exact today, so adopting it needs a per-loop check first
_withdrawn.status: withdrawn (W9r10 review D4, 2026-10-21): N76 records a candidate rule backed by 13 kernels, so by the notes' own evidence the design is not shown to be unfixable; it stays open work until the per-loop check of N76 (10 of the 14 corpus designs with the [HLS 200-960] warning are exact today) has been done

_withdrawn.status: withdrawn again (W9 round 12 review defect 4, 2026-10-22): the W9r12-prove proposal said '20 kernels have not found which source shape triggers it, so no general rule can be stated', but N76 states a candidate rule backed by 13 kernels (automatic pipeline only, a sub-loop unrolled only by that pipeline, no branch on the child's or sub-loop's index) and its next step, the per-loop check of the corpus designs that print [HLS 200-960], has not been done; the design stays open work until that check (the W9r10 review D4 withdrawal, above, still applies)
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope_proposed_w9r12: Vitis refuses the flatten with [HLS 200-960] '... either the parent loop or sub loop is do-while loop', a loop rotation in the closed front end; 20 kernels (N64 / N76) have not found which source shape triggers it, so no general rule can be stated (W9r12-prove: the only DoD-5 straggler proposed; every other out-of-band class has a proven or known mechanism)

_withdrawn.cause: `V` and `scores` 1 each against Vitis 2 (-2): the loop reads 4 elements per state at II 4 in Vitis (two ports bound), hls-est spreads the reads over the II and binds one port
_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: W9r16-prove ranked list (`~/hls-est-work/coord/scratch/w9r16p/ranked.md`): Vitis memory rows V / scores RAM_2P 2 each; the read placement per state is read from the schedule report, no kernel reproduces it
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: the rule (why Vitis places 4 reads in one state of an II 4 loop) is not proven by a kernel; modelling the corpus case alone would be overfitting
_withdrawn.status: withdrawn (W9 round 16 review defect 6, 2026-10-23): the entry said no kernel reproduces it, but no kernel was tried; open work (OPEN_ISSUES O168): build a kernel with 4 reads of one array per iteration of an II 4 loop and read the schedule report

_withdrawn.cause: `I_minus_BZ_A_inverse` 1 against Vitis 2 (-1): Vitis pipelines loop 1180_20, hls-est leaves it sequential (one port); `sort_client_list` is a name difference only (1 = 1)
_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: Vitis loop table of GP_selection (VITIS_LOOP_1180_20 pipelined), memory row I_minus_BZ_A_inverse RAM_2P 2 (W9r16-prove ranked list)
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: why Vitis pipelines that loop (no pragma; the automatic pipeline decision of N3 says no) is not proven by a kernel
_withdrawn.status: withdrawn (W9 round 16 review defect 5, 2026-10-23): the entry said the rule was not proven by a kernel, but the loop table flattens VITIS_LOOP_1180_20_VITIS_LOOP_1182_21_VITIS_LOOP_1184_22 and the 20-line kernel w9r16rv_gp_flat (a perfect nest with run-time bounds, M[i][j] += in the pipelined k loop: Vitis 2, M 1R1W) reproduces the -1. Fixed in the review-fix round (VITIS_NOTES N129: flatten_nest_invariant_bounds, promote_nest_invariant_only; GP_selection fixed 66 -> 67 = Vitis)

_withdrawn.cause: `weights` (an array of a struct element) 0 against Vitis 3 (hls-est does not estimate the struct element) and FIFO rows +2: net -1 of 20,600
_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: W9r16-prove ranked list: Vitis memory row weights 3 BRAM; hls-est's debug JSON has no memref for the struct member
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: the struct-element splitting of this design's weights (a nested aggregate) is not implemented and no kernel isolates it; 0.005 % of the design
_withdrawn.status: withdrawn (W9 round 16 review defect 6, 2026-10-23): 'struct element not estimated' is an hls-est implementation gap (no memref for the struct member weights, -3, offset by FIFO rows +2), not an unproven Vitis rule; open work (OPEN_ISSUES O169)

_withdrawn.cause: `tmp_buf` 2 against Vitis 4 (64-bit buffer RAM_1P 2 against ram_t2p 4): Vitis binds two ports because the two stores of the `unroll factor=2` copies issue in the same state of the II > 1 pipeline; hls-est's modulo schedule puts them in different slots
_withdrawn.vitis_evidence: VITIS_NOTES N119: the schedule reports (`db/*Pipeline_L*.verbose.sched.rpt`) of atax (II 15, both tmp_buf stores in state 878), atax-medium (II 49, state 2884) and gesummv-medium (II 30, y_buf stores in state 1790); kernel w9r15p_st2_w (the same loop shape, Vitis puts the stores in different states, ram_1p 2 = hls-est): the state follows each stored value's ready time W9r17-prove (VITIS_NOTES N133): Vitis' dadd and dmul take 7 states at 10 ns (`[7/7]`, 7.29 / 6.71 ns) and the two copies' chains run in lockstep (both `add` chains start in ST_10; atax's stores both in ST_878, atax-medium's in 2884, gesummv-medium's `y_buf` in 1790); with a private configuration giving hls-est the same 7-cycle latencies (`w9r17p/n119/lat7.json`) its stores land within 2-6 cycles of Vitis' state but the two copies stay 7-24 cycles apart (876 / 883, 2878 / 2902, 1772 / 1786), (lat7). W9 round 17 review fixes (VITIS_NOTES N133 corrected, OPEN_ISSUES O181): the copies' chains were apart because hls-est's greedy scheduler gave the loads' port slots in program order (copy 1's loads first), not because adders were shared (the modulo problem limits no FP operator). Vitis interleaves the copies' loads (kernel w9r17fx_hp: one load per copy per state, both t stores in ST_66, ram_t2p 4) and a height priority in the greedy scheduler reproduces that and makes atax and atax-medium exact; but in the same catalogue run bicg (q_buf ST_823 / 824), gesummv (tmp_buf 641 / 643, y_buf 671 / 672) and gesummv-medium's tmp_buf (1761 / 1762) show that Vitis does not always end the copies in one state, and they lose their per-array agreement (run w9r17fx/Y: exact 707 -> 706).
_withdrawn.why_out_of_scope: the state of each copy's store follows Vitis' port-slot order among the copies' loads; the rule found (height priority, `scheduling.modulo.height_priority`) is right for this design and the kernel but wrong for bicg x 3 and gesummv, so it stays off (working-loop rule 4) until O181 finds what offsets the second copy there.
_withdrawn.status: withdrawn (W9r18-impl (2026-10-23): the cause is proven and implemented (VITIS_NOTES N135: Vitis gives each floating-point class ceil(ops / II) units and places the body in height order; scheduling.modulo.fp_unit_limits and height_priority, on): exact in the final W9r18-impl run.)
